title: Mercy
lead: Mercy is kindness to people in need or in the wrong, including people who deserve judgment. "Merciful and gracious" is how God describes himself to Moses at Sinai (Exodus 34:6).

sections.b: God declares himself "The LORD, the LORD, a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger" (Exodus 34:6), words repeated through the Old Testament (Psalm 103:8; Jonah 4:2). In the Greek Old Testament, eleos, "mercy," often translates the Hebrew hesed, God's loyal, covenant love; for that word, see the hesed page. This page is about the idea of mercy across the Bible.

"Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy" (Matthew 5:7). Jesus quotes Hosea, "I desire mercy, not sacrifice" (Matthew 9:13; 12:7; Hosea 6:6), and the parable of the unforgiving servant asks, "Shouldn't you have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?" (Matthew 18:33). James says "mercy triumphs over judgment" (James 2:13).
sections.refs: Matthew 5:7; Matthew 9:13; Matthew 18:33; Hosea 6:6; Luke 6:36; James 2:13
